The growth is driven by the accelerating integration of IoT and blockchain technologies, which are reshaping supply chains into highly connected, intelligent ecosystems. IoT-enabled sensors provide real-time visibility into shipment conditions, asset locations, and production metrics, allowing proactive intervention and continuous optimization. Simultaneously, blockchain ensures data authenticity and transactional transparency across multi-tier supplier networks, reducing compliance burdens and building stakeholder trust. These capabilities empower businesses to minimize losses, shorten lead times, and increase operational agility, making advanced SCM solutions indispensable in today’s global and volatile trade environment. The growing complexity of global logistics and rising freight costs are driving demand for cloud-based transportation management systems, offering route optimization, real-time visibility, and cost-efficient, resilient supply chains. Impact of AI on Supply Chain Management (SCM) Market Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Generative AI (GenAI) transforms the supply chain management market by enabling real-time decision-making, predictive analytics, and intelligent automation. These technologies enhance demand forecasting, optimize logistics, and streamline procurement processes. AI and GenAI are reshaping traditional supply chains into agile, data-driven ecosystems that respond swiftly to market changes by reducing human error and increasing operational efficiency. Global Supply Chain Management (SCM) Market Dynamics Driver: Demand for greater visibility and transparency in supply chain data and processes Historically, fragmented data and unconnected systems have limited visibility across supply chains, reducing forecasting accuracy, delaying reaction to disruptions, and resulting in costly inventory imbalances. In the digital age, supply chain leaders gradually recognize end-to-end transparency as a strategic requirement. According to the Maersk Survey 2024, 77% of global enterprises invest in visibility-enhancing tools to strengthen agility and risk management. However, the GEODIS Supply Chain Worldwide Survey highlights that only 6% of companies currently report having complete visibility over their supply chains, revealing a critical operational gap. To address this gap, enterprises rapidly implement AI, IoT, machine learning, and blockchain to unify data streams via intelligent "control towers." These technologies offer real-time asset tracking, predictive risk alarms, and secure transaction records. The growing demand for such integrated visibility is reshaping operational models and emerging as a fundamental force driving the widespread adoption of supply chain management solutions across industries. Restraint: Growing security and privacy concerns among enterprises Security and privacy concerns continue to hinder the adoption of cloud-based supply chain management (SCM) solutions. These platforms often operate in multitenant architectures, where shared environments increase the risk of data leakage, cross-tenant breaches, and misconfigured access. According to Netgain Technologies, 27% of businesses experienced a public cloud security incident in 2024, representing a 10% increase over 2023, signaling growing exposure to cloud vulnerabilities. Further, the 2024 Thales Cloud Security Study reports that 44% of surveyed organizations experienced cloud-related breaches, with most incidents attributed to insecure identities and poor access management. These persistent weaknesses and limited real-time monitoring across many enterprises erode trust, elevate regulatory risk, and hinder broader SCM cloud platform adoption. Opportunity: Government R&D investment initiatives for robust advancements in supply chain management solutions Government-backed R&D initiatives are pivotal in accelerating technological innovation across supply chain management. With increased focus on digital infrastructure, public investments support integrating advanced technologies such as IoT, 5G, AI, blockchain, robotics, and 3D printing into modern SCM systems. These technologies form the foundation of next-generation digital supply networks by enhancing transparency, traceability, and responsiveness across the value chain. For instance, IoT-enabled sensors now provide real-time tracking of asset location and shipment conditions, allowing logistics teams to make proactive, data-driven decisions. Currently, 80% of logistics firms deploy AI for delay prediction and route optimization, while over 60% of manufacturers use IoT for production oversight. Such R&D-backed advancements enable smarter, more agile supply chains, paving the way for enhanced resilience, risk mitigation, and service quality. Challenge: Limited awareness about supply chain management techniques The lack of understanding and awareness of modern SCM techniques is a key barrier to the growth of supply chain management, particularly in industries such as healthcare. Many professionals are still unaware with the full possibilities of integrated SCM systems, and they continue to rely on antiquated methods like Just-In-Time (JIT) inventory or basic stockless models. While these methods offer some benefits, they lack the efficiency, responsiveness, and cost control of contemporary, data-driven SCM platforms. Without sufficient executive backing and cross-departmental awareness, organizations often operate in silos, resulting in poor coordination, limited data sharing, and fragmented decision-making. To build agile, outcome-focused supply chains, there is a pressing need for structured employee training, access to real-time data, and integrated communication systems that reinforce the strategic role of SCM. Source: Secondary Research and MarketsandMarkets Analysis Based on software, the purchasing management software segment is expected to dominate the market during the forecast period. Purchase management software holds the largest share in the supply chain management (SCM) market due to its pivotal role in driving cost efficiency, inventory accuracy, and vendor coordination across industries. This software enables businesses to control procurement-related expenses, manage supplier relationships, and maintain optimal stock levels, thereby reducing holding costs and ensuring timely replenishment. Improving visibility across purchasing activities and automating workflows supports better cash flow management, mitigates contractual risks, and provides consistent product availability. Its ability to directly impact profitability makes it indispensable for enterprise operations. The segment’s depth, encompassing procurement, capital purchasing, strategic sourcing, and transportation management, further reinforces its dominance as organizations increasingly prioritize data-driven, cost-effective purchasing strategies within their SCM frameworks. The RFID Tags and Readers hardware segment is expected to grow at the highest CAGR during the forecast period. RFID tags and readers are expected to witness the fastest growth in the SCM market due to their ability to significantly enhance real-time visibility, automation, and inventory control. Unlike traditional barcodes, RFID does not require line-of-sight and enables remote scanning of tagged items, streamlining operations from production to distribution. This technology improves traceability, prevents theft, reduces human error, and supports automation in critical tasks such as receiving, shipping, and validation. RFID minimizes item misplacement and lowers operational costs by enabling accurate, instant product identification. The demand for greater transparency, security, and speed drives its growing adoption across warehousing, retail, and healthcare supply chains. As enterprises prioritize intelligent, data-driven supply networks, RFID remains a key enabler of efficient SCM practices. With manufacturing, retail, and healthcare industries heavily investing in consulting, support, and cloud-based tools, North America continues to lead global SCM innovation and deployment.
